mainTopic: Releasing a נדר before it takes effect; then a משנה on wives' claims that end a marriage, with a כהן's wife's eating of תרומה and her כתובה
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a sugya about whether a חכם can release a נדר before it takes effect. One version of the dispute between רבי נתן and רבנן says everyone agrees he can. The גמרא tests that version against two ברייתות. The first ברייתא is answered, because it never says which vow counts as 'first.' The second ברייתא, about a vow and a linked נזירות, fixes the order clearly, so that version is refuted with a תיובתא. A new משנה follows about three claims a wife might make to end her marriage. At first she was believed and collected her כתובה, but חכמים later changed the rule so a woman could not invent an excuse to leave. The גמרא then asks whether a כהן's wife who says 'I am defiled' may eat תרומה. רב ששת says she may and רבא says she may not, and רבא adds that רב ששת agrees she may not once she is widowed or divorced. Finally, רבא's test question asks whether a כהן's wife who was raped still gets her כתובה, and the discussion continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Spelling out what the previous version implies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out what the version just quoted means: the vow had no effect yet, only words, and it could still be released.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is to say, there was no action in it yet. The vow was only spoken words, and it can still be released.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is spelling out what the version it just quoted implies. This sets up the challenges that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The version just quoted holds that everyone agrees a חכם can release a vow even before it has taken effect. This line makes that point explicit: there was no 'action' yet, only words. The next steps test this claim against ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: That is to say; this shows that
Action; here, the vow actually taking effect
Asking a חכם to release a vow

phrases.english: That is to say, there was no action in it.
phrases.notes: He means the vow hadn't kicked in yet; it was only words, and still a חכם could release it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes out the version quoted just before this section by drawing out its meaning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this version, a vow that has not yet taken effect can still be released by a חכם.

steps.title: Challenge from the vow against the sage he will ask
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא requires asking about the first vow before the second. If vows could be released before taking effect, why not let him choose either order?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: Someone said, 'It is קונם for me to benefit from So-and-so, and from whichever person I ask to release me from this vow.' The ruling is that he asks about the first vow, and afterward he asks about the second. But why? If he wants, he could ask about this one first, and if he wants, he could ask about that one first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the version from step 1 using a ברייתא about two linked vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second vow (not to benefit from the חכם he asks) only takes effect once he asks about the first vow. If a vow can be released before it takes effect, he should be free to start with either one. Since the ברייתא sets an order, it seems a vow cannot be released before it takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא)
A word used to make something forbidden like a קרבן; a standard vow word
So-and-so
Let him ask first

phrases.english: They raised an objection: 'Konam, that I will not benefit from so-and-so,
and from whoever I will ask about it' —
phrases.notes: He also forbids himself to benefit from the חכם he will go to for release of the first vow.

phrases.english: he asks about the first,
and afterward he asks about the second.

phrases.aramaic: אַמַּאי? אִי בָּעֵי — עַל הַאי נִיתְּשִׁיל בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: Why? If he wants, let him ask about this one first,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בָּעֵי — עַל הַאי נִיתְּשִׁיל בְּרֵישָׁא!
phrases.english: and if he wants, let him ask about that one first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim made in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version holding that everyone agrees a vow can be released before it takes effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires a fixed order, which only makes sense if the not-yet-active second vow cannot be released first.

steps.title: The ברייתא never says which vow is first
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the words 'first' and 'second' do not tell us which vow is which, so he may really be able to start with either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who knows which one is 'first' and which one is 'second'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the version by pointing out that the ברייתא is not clear about the order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only says 'first' and then 'second.' It does not say which vow is which. So 'first' could mean whichever vow he picks to start with, including the vow about the חכם. That fits the view that a vow can be released before it takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Who knows? (here: it is not clear)
Which

phrases.aramaic: מִי יוֹדֵעַ הֵי רִאשׁוֹן וְהֵי שֵׁנִי?
phrases.english: Who knows which is first and which is second?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי יוֹדֵעַ הֵי רִאשׁוֹן וְהֵי שֵׁנִי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the ברייתא: its order is not fixed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא requires the vow against So-and-so first and the vow against the חכם second.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'First' and 'second' are not defined, so either vow may be released first.

steps.title: Challenge from the vow linked to נזירות
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא clearly requires asking about the vow first and the נזירות second, even though the נזירות only starts once he asks.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged again: Someone said, 'It is קונם for me to benefit from this, and I am a נזיר once I ask a חכם to release me from this vow.' The ruling is that he asks about his vow, and afterward he asks about his נזירות. But why? If he wants, he could ask about his vow first, and if he wants, he could ask about his נזירות first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא, where the order is spelled out clearly, to challenge the version again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the ברייתא names the two vows: first his נדר, then his נזירות. The נזירות only takes effect when he asks about the first vow. If a vow could be released before it takes effect, he could clear the נזירות first. The answer from step 3 does not work here, because the order is explicit.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who has taken a vow of נזירות (no wine, no haircut, no contact with the dead)
When I will ask (for release)
His vow
His vow of נזירות

phrases.english: They raised an objection: 'Konam, that I will not benefit,
and I am hereby a nazir once I ask about it' —
he asks about his vow,
and afterward he asks about his naziriteship.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַמַּאי? אִי בָּעֵי — עַל נִדְרוֹ נִיתְּשִׁיל בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: But why? If he wants, let him ask about his vow first,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בָּעֵי — עַל נִזְרוֹ נִיתְּשִׁיל בְּרֵישָׁא!
phrases.english: and if he wants, let him ask about his naziriteship first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge that gets around the answer of step 3, because here the order is explicit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version holding that a vow can be released before it takes effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא fixes the order: the vow first, then the נזירות. That means the not-yet-active נזירות cannot be released ahead of time.

steps.title: The version is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a תיובתא: this version of the dispute is refuted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits there is no answer to the second ברייתא, so the version from step 1 is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order in the second ברייתא cannot be read away. So the claim that everyone agrees a vow can be released before it takes effect does not stand.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; the view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: This version, where everyone agrees a vow can be released before it takes effect, is refuted. The ברייתא about the vow and the נזירות shows that a vow which has not yet taken effect cannot be released ahead of time.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two challenges. The first one was answered because 'first' and 'second' were unclear. The second one fails to be answered because the ברייתא names exactly which vow comes first.

phrases.english: A refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms that the challenge of step 4 has no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The version holding that everyone agrees a vow can be released before it takes effect is rejected.

steps.title: The original rule: three women who leave and collect their כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a new topic. At first, חכמים ruled that a woman making any of three claims leaves the marriage and still collects her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they used to say: three women go out of the marriage and collect their כתובה. One who says 'I am defiled to you,' one who says 'Heaven is between me and you,' and one who says 'I am removed from the Jews.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It reports the earlier rule: three kinds of claims let a wife end the marriage and still get her כתובה money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each claim makes it seem that the couple can no longer live together. A כהן's wife says she was violated, so she is forbidden to him. Another wife says he cannot be with her. A third made a vow against all Jews. Under the first rule she is believed, and the husband must divorce her and pay.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
At first, originally
The money a husband owes his wife when the marriage ends
'I am defiled to you': forbidden to my husband
'I am removed from the Jews': a vow against relations with any Jew

phrases.english: MISHNA:
At first they used to say:
Three women go out of the marriage and collect their marriage contract:
one who says, 'I am defiled to you,'
phrases.notes: This is a כהן's wife claiming she was violated, so she is now forbidden to him.

phrases.english: 'Heaven is between me and you,'
phrases.notes: She claims he cannot be with her. Only Heaven knows if that is true.

phrases.english: and 'I am removed from the Jews.'
phrases.notes: A vow forbidding herself to every Jewish man, her husband included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the previous sugya ended in a תיובתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally, a wife making any of the three claims was divorced and collected her כתובה.

steps.title: The later rule: protecting the husband from false claims
steps.stepSummary: חכמים changed the rule so that a wife who wants another man cannot ruin her marriage with a claim nobody can check. Each of the three cases gets a new rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: They changed their ruling, so that a woman would not set her eyes on another man and ruin things with her husband. One who says 'I am defiled to you' must bring proof. For 'Heaven is between me and you,' they handle it by making a request. For 'I am removed from the Jews,' he cancels his part, she may live with him, and she stays forbidden to other Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the later rule. חכמים worried that women might make false claims to get out of the marriage, so they took away the easy exit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'defiled' claim now needs proof. The 'Heaven' claim no longer forces a divorce; בית דין only asks the husband to divorce her. In the vow case, the husband cancels only the part that affects him. She stays permitted to him but forbidden to everyone else, so she gains nothing by leaving.

keyTerms.meaning: They changed their ruling
Ruins things with her husband
By way of a request, not by force
He cancels his part of her vow

steps.whatToRemember: The later rule stops a wife from using an unprovable claim to escape her marriage and still collect her כתובה.

phrases.english: They went back and said,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא אִשָּׁה נוֹתֶנֶת עֵינֶיהָ בְּאַחֵר
phrases.english: so that a woman should not set her eyes on another man
and ruin things with her husband:
one who says 'I am defiled to you'
must bring proof for her words.
'Heaven is between me and you':
they should handle it by way of a request.
phrases.notes: בית דין asks the husband to divorce her. They do not force him.

phrases.english: And 'I am removed from the Jews':
he should cancel his part,
phrases.notes: The husband cancels the vow only as far as it affects him.

phrases.english: and she may be with him as his wife,
and she stays removed from the other Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the original rule from step 6 with a stricter one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Later rule: a 'defiled' claim needs proof, a 'Heaven' claim only leads to a request, and in the vow case the husband cancels his part and the marriage continues.

steps.title: May a כהן's wife who says 'I am defiled' eat תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: we do not believe her enough to end the marriage, but may she still eat תרומה?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if she told her husband 'I am defiled,' may she eat תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about the later rule. It sets up a disagreement that comes in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the later rule she is not believed enough to force a divorce. But a כהן's wife who was with another man may not eat תרומה. So does her own word at least stop her from eating it?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים
Holy produce that only כהנים and their households may eat
The discussion that follows the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
A question was raised before them:
If she said to her husband, 'I am defiled,'
what is the law about her eating תרומה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the later rule in the משנה (step 7), that she must bring proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether her own unproven claim of being defiled forbids her to eat תרומה, even though it does not end the marriage.

steps.title: רב ששת: she may eat, to protect her children
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that she may eat תרומה, so that people will not start rumors about her children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: she may eat, so that she does not bring a bad name on her children.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives the first answer: she may keep eating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people saw her stop eating תרומה, they would think her claim was true. Then they might wonder whether her children are really her husband's and fit for כהונה. To prevent that rumor, she keeps eating.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who rules that she may eat
A bad rumor
She may eat

phrases.english: רב ששת said: She may eat,
so that she not bring out a bad rumor about her children.
phrases.notes: People might think her sons are not really her husband's and so not fit to be כהנים.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She may eat תרומה, to keep rumors away from her children.

steps.title: רבא: she may not eat, since she can eat regular food
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees and says she may not eat תרומה. She loses nothing, because she can eat ordinary food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: she may not eat, because she can eat ordinary food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite answer: she should not eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא takes her claim seriously enough to keep her away from תרומה. Avoiding it costs her nothing, because ordinary food is easy to get. He does not let the worry about rumors outweigh that.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who rules that she may not eat
Ordinary food that is not holy

phrases.english: רבא said: She may not eat,
since it is possible for her to eat ordinary food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an answer that argues with רב ששת in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She may not eat תרומה, since she can eat ordinary food instead.

steps.title: רב ששת agrees she may not eat once widowed or divorced
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that רב ששת's reason only holds while she is married. Once she is widowed or divorced, no rumor reaches her children, so even רב ששת forbids her to eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב ששת agrees that if she became a widow, she may not eat. His only reason was the bad rumor about her children. Once she is widowed or divorced, people will say: she was only violated now.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows where רב ששת's lenient ruling stops. Its own reason does not reach a woman who is widowed or divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת let her eat only to protect her children. After the marriage ends, people would assume anything that happened to her happened later. Then the children born during the marriage are not under suspicion, so the reason is gone and she may not eat.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees
She became a widow
Is the reason anything other than
She was violated, forced

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's permission depends only on protecting the children. Once she is widowed or divorced, that worry is gone and both agree she may not eat תרומה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not taking back his own view here. He is showing that even רב ששת, who allows her to eat during the marriage, agrees with him after the marriage ends.

phrases.english: רבא said:
And רב ששת agrees
that if she became a widow, she may not eat.
Is the reason anything

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם תּוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל בָּנֶיהָ.
phrases.english: other than that she would bring a bad rumor about her children?
Once she is widowed or divorced,
people will say: it was only now that she was violated.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רַב שֵׁשֶׁת שֶׁאִם נִתְאַרְמְלָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ אוֹכֶלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב ששת's ruling from step 9 using his own reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even רב ששת agrees that a widowed or divorced woman who claimed to be defiled may not eat תרומה, since the reason about rumors no longer applies.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a ruling based on one specific reason ends where that reason ends.

steps.title: רבא's test question about a כהן's wife who was raped
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reports that רבא tested the students: does a כֹּהֵן's wife who was raped receive her כתובה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: רבא tested us. If the wife of a כֹּהֵן was raped, does she get her כתובה payment or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question. רבא tested his students, asking whether a כֹּהֵן's wife who was raped still gets her כתובה money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כֹּהֵן may not stay married to a wife who was with another man, even against her will. So this marriage must end. The question is whether she still collects the money her כתובה promises her when it ends.

keyTerms.meaning: He tested us. A teacher asks his students a question to check how well they think.
The wife of a כֹּהֵן (a priest)
She was forced (raped). It happened against her will.
The marriage contract. It promises the wife money if the marriage ends.

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody blames her here. The question is only about money. Her marriage has to end because of the special rules for a כֹּהֵן, so does she still collect her כתובה?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Rava tested us:
The wife of a priest who was raped,
does she receive her marriage contract payment
or does she not receive her marriage contract payment?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, בָּדֵיק לַן רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the תרומה discussion. It stays with the same subject of a woman who becomes forbidden to her husband.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a כֹּהֵן's wife who was raped, and must therefore leave her husband, still collects her כתובה.

steps.title: The two sides of רבא's question
steps.stepSummary: Side one: for a כֹּהֵן, rape counts like willing sin does for a ישראל, so she loses her כתובה. Side two begins: maybe she can say, 'I myself am fit.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Since being raped makes a woman forbidden to a כֹּהֵן, just as willing sin makes a woman forbidden to a ישראל, maybe she gets no כתובה. Or perhaps she can tell him: 'I am fit...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is hard by showing the two ways to see it. The second side is cut off in the middle. It continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one compares her to a ישראל's wife who sinned willingly. That woman must leave her husband and loses her כתובה, so the כֹּהֵן's wife should lose hers too. Side two says she can claim that she herself is still fit for marriage. Married to a ישראל, she would not be forbidden at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Something done by force, against her will
Something done willingly, by her own choice
Or perhaps. This phrase brings in the other side of a question.
I am fit. She means she is still suitable for marriage.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: is her loss of the כתובה tied to her own act, or to her husband's special status as a כֹּהֵן?

phrases.english: Since rape, with regard to a priest,
is like willing relations with regard to an Israelite,
phrases.notes: In both cases the woman becomes forbidden to her husband and must leave him.

phrases.english: she does not receive her marriage contract payment.
Or perhaps she can say to him:
I am indeed fit,
phrases.notes: Her sentence isn't finished yet. It continues on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאוֹנֶס לְגַבֵּי כֹּהֵן כְּרָצוֹן לְגַבֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question asked in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side is right: is her case like willing sin, so she loses the כתובה, or can she claim she herself is still fit, so she keeps it?
